mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level, accompanied by a concurrent decline in CPIAUCSL, signals a premature tightening that compresses growth expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥ 0.25 percentage points relative to previous month and CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 0.2% in the same month.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite the trigger, or FEDFUNDS increase is not confirmed by CPIAUCSL decline in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently above 4.00% for three consecutive months, it creates a risk premium that elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher future rates.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during the high-rate window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in PAYEMS (labor market additions) followed by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests a strengthening labor market that boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 2% month-over-month and UNRATE decreases by ≥ 0.2 percentage points in the same month.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified labor strength episode.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of at least 10% followed by a rebound above the prior low is interpreted as a bottoming signal, which tends to precede a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops for two consecutive months then rises in the third month by ≥ 12% from the prior low.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat during the identified recovery window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 5% in a month, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in GDPC1 (nominal GDP), predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as supply-side weakness depresses earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥ 5% and GDPC1 falls by ≥ 2% in the same month.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months in a labor market expansion regime, it signals tighter labor constraints and tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for two consecutive months and the regime_hint is 'labor market expansion'.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (money supply growth) for three consecutive months, without a corresponding drop in FEDFUNDS, is interpreted as a loss of monetary accommodation and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥ 1% for three consecutive months and FEDFUNDS does not fall in the same period.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative despite the contraction, or FEDFUNDS declines in parallel with RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in GDPC1 growth (second derivative > 0) exceeding 2% per month, while HOUST remains flat or declining, suggests strong and sustained demand that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Second difference of GDPC1 > 2% per month and HOUST does not increase by ≥ 3% in the same month.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified acceleration.
